PullRequest.Title: test: stop auto-hiding scrollbars from flashing in fixture screenshots
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Fixes the flaky `sessions/chatCompositeBar/MixedStatuses/Light` screenshot reported in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/342258#issuecomment-6232874847, and the same class of flake across all component fixtures.

## Why

Auto-hiding (`ScrollbarVisibility.Auto`) scrollbars reveal on every scroll event. `Scrollable._setState` fires `onScroll` for scroll-dimension changes too, so any layout change (typically from a native `ResizeObserver` callback that runs outside the fixture's virtual clock) reveals the scrollbar, which then hides after a real 500ms timer. Whether a headless screenshot caught it was down to timing. Fixtures had accumulated ad-hoc workarounds for this: waiting for `.scrollbar.invisible`, `style.visibility = 'hidden'`, fixed sleeps, and extended virtual time.

## What

- `scrollableElement.ts`: a test-only `disableScrollbarRevealOnScroll()` seam (reference-counted, modeled on `installFakeRunWhenIdle`). While active, `_onDidScroll` does not reveal scrollbars. Hover/drag reveal and `ScrollbarVisibility.Visible` scrollbars are unaffected; production behavior is unchanged.
- `fixtureUtils.ts`: install it for headless renders only (CI / CLI / MCP screenshots). The interactive explorer keeps real behavior.
- Removed the per-fixture scrollbar workarounds in `chatRendering`, `chatScrollAnchoring`, `connectionDiagnostics`, `chatPetAchievementsEditor`, `sessionActivityBar`, and `aiCustomizationManagementEditor`.
- Updated the component-fixtures skill: don't wait for or hide auto-hiding scrollbars; use `ScrollbarVisibility.Visible` when a scrollbar is part of the intended state.

## Validation

- `component-explorer render --fixture-id-regex '/Light$'` (as CI does) for all 1696 fixtures, twice on `main` and twice with this change:
  - No new fixture errors (the 14 existing `chatReferences`/`buttonBar` errors are unchanged).
  - 13 images change vs. `main`. 12 only lose an 8–10px scrollbar strip on the right/bottom edge that both `main` runs captured mid-reveal. 1 (`BulkDoneNotificationAnimated`) is a 4px pre-existing noise diff that reproduces with `main` when rendered in isolation.
  - None of the changed fixtures are in `blocks-ci-screenshots.md`.
  - Run-to-run stable apart from the already-noisy `chatGeneratedImages` fixtures.
- `component-explorer check_stability` on all `chatCompositeBar` fixtures: 39/39 stable.
- `npm run eslint` on the changed files: passed. `tsc -p src/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: no errors in changed files (pre-existing unrelated `src/vs/platform/agentHost` errors from a local dependency mismatch).

Scenarios.Scenario: Headless component-fixture rendering and screenshot capture across the fixture suite
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fixture setup installs the reference-counted suppression, component rendering and virtual-time settling complete, then the host captures the screenshot. Scroll events still update/render scrollbar geometry but now skip reveal CSS transitions and the 500 ms hide timer; fixture disposal releases the suppression.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One suppression handle per concurrently mounted headless fixture; scroll handling scales with layout/scroll events and the number of scrollable elements. The counter makes overlapping fixtures constant-time per event without per-scroll allocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Potentially overlapping headless fixtures share one global reference count; each fixture contributes one handle, so suppression remains active until the last overlapping fixture is disposed. No queue, IPC, subprocess, or remote-operation concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or cache key is changed. Cold and warm fixture behavior differ only through pre-existing theme/assets setup; scrollbar suppression is deterministic in both states.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added condition is directly on _onDidScroll, _reveal creates scrollbar transitions and schedules the hide timer, and fixtureUtils gates suppression to headless hosts with lifecycle disposal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact scroll-event counts and fixture overlap depend on the runner, but the changed work is a constant integer check and removes reveal/timer work rather than adding scaling cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The diff removes timer/transition work from the headless screenshot critical path and adds only a constant branch per scroll event.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering the modified chat, diagnostics, achievements, and AI customization screenshot fixtures
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each fixture renders its intended state, performs existing layout/content readiness checks, and resolves before screenshot capture. Deleted scrollbar polling, computed-style reads, DOM scans, and fixed waits no longer delay capture.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work previously scaled with readiness frames, scrollbar count, and fixed delays (including up to 2.4 seconds for scrolled MCP fixtures); the diff reduces those costs and does not add replacement work beyond one animation frame where needed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fixture-local async waits remain coordinated by their existing render promises. The diff removes polling/sleep serialization and introduces no new parallel burst or limiter interaction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No caches are used or changed by the removed waits. Marketplace/content setup remains pre-existing and unchanged; neither success nor failure cache behavior is modified.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every modified fixture hunk deletes readiness conditions or sleeps tied only to scrollbar fade state, with no added expensive operation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual wall-clock savings vary because virtual time and real browser frames differ by fixture, but all changed mechanisms remove critical-path waits or DOM/style checks.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; fixture latency and repeated DOM/style work are reduced.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: A scroll event updates scrollbar state, checks revealOnScrollDisabledCount, reveals auto-hiding scrollbars when the count is zero, and renders as before. Interactive explorer fixtures do not install suppression; production code has no caller that installs it.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One added integer comparison per scroll event regardless of document or collection size; reveal/render cardinality is unchanged when suppression is inactive.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new asynchronous work or concurrency is introduced. The module-level count is synchronously incremented/decremented only by explicitly opted-in headless fixture lifetimes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: repository search found the sole suppression caller in headless-gated fixture setup, while hover/drag reveal and ordinary production scroll reveal remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Scroll frequency can be high, but a single predictable integer comparison is too small to establish actionable CPU, rendering, or latency impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The production hot path gains only a constant guard and preserves the existing reveal/render operations.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files and all diff pages. Traced headless fixture setup/disposal, scrollbar scroll/reveal/render behavior, removed readiness polling and sleeps, interactive gating, lifecycle ownership, concurrency, caches, and expensive boundaries. The change reduces screenshot critical-path work and introduces no actionable performance regression.
